messages:
evelyn (customer): hi — we've started seeing intermittent JSON.parse failures from the streaming /v1/streams endpoint after yesterday's deploy. ~1-2% of responses arrive truncated and client throws 'Unexpected end of JSON input'.

Here's one of the raw tail fragments we got (copied from client):
```json
{"id":"resp_9f3a","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"reply\":\"Here are the results:\\n- item1\\n- item2\\n\"},\"meta\":{\"cursor\":12345"}]}]
```
(note: it just cuts off after the cursor field, no closing braces)

maria (support): thanks — sorry you're hitting this. are you using structured/json mode or function-calling? any middle proxies or auth token refresh in the path? can you paste minimal repro steps?

evelyn (customer): using structured JSON mode (mode=json) with SSE-style streaming. no function-calling. traffic hits our api-gateway (nginx) -> cloud-lb -> redwood edge. we do rotate tokens via short-lived creds, but token rotation happens client-side every 10m. repro steps i used locally:
```bash
# reproducer (curl streaming)
export TOKEN=***
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"generate structured reply","mode":"json","stream":true}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams"
```
It sometimes produces a truncated final chunk after ~18-40s.

kevin (sre): @maria @evelyn a couple of thoughts: 1) truncated JSON on stream usually means an upstream connection close (FIN/RST) or an intermediate proxy timeout mid-chunk. 2) short-lived token rotation can cause mid-request auth failures if the gateway revalidates on keepalive. can you capture tcpdump at the nginx -> lb hop and check for FIN or RST pairs? also check nginx error.log for `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `broken pipe`.

jonathan (eng-ml): dev note: on the serving side the runtime emits chunks as soon as kv-cache or tokens are available; we expect proxies to preserve chunk boundaries. if a FIN arrives mid-chunk the client will obviously see invalid JSON. temporary app-level workaround: buffer chunks and only attempt JSON.parse after braces balance, or accept newline-delimited json objects rather than a single nested object. i'll follow up on possible sentinel/footer options.

maria (support): eve — can you try two quick tests for us: 1) reproduce with curl but add `--no-buffer` and `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` to see if behavior changes; 2) reproduce with a direct connection that bypasses your nginx (point client at the lb / edge if possible). also include a full tcpdump snippet if you have it.

evelyn (customer): did both. relevant tcpdump snippet (cut):
```
15:03:12.123 IP client.34567 > lb.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12478, ack 9876, win 501, length 133
15:03:30.876 IP lb.443 > client.34567: Flags [FIN, ACK], seq 8877, ack 12478, win 501, length 0
# saw FIN from LB ~17s after stream start, right in the middle of a JSON object
```
also tried direct-to-edge (bypassing nginx) and saw lower rate of truncation but still some occurrences.

kevin (sre): that FIN from lb is suspicious — suggests LB idle/socket window maybe closing after 17s. check LB idle timeout (classic ELBs sometimes have default 60s but some infra set shorter). also check if LB is health-checking and resetting backend sockets. another quick diagn: set `Expect: 100-continue` off or toggle `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` behavior.

jonathan (eng-ml): also adding: runtime currently doesn't append an explicit end-of-json sentinel in streaming json mode (we rely on full connection close to signal completion). short-term we can patch runtime to emit a small final marker `{"__redwood_stream_end":true}` as last delta so clients can detect truncation vs normal end. i'll open an eng ticket.

maria (support): i've raised a priority handoff to eng-infra with these logs and the tcpdump snippet. @kevin can you pull LB logs and check for any backend resets matching that timestamp? i'll keep a note for the billing/auth team too in case token refresh is involved.

kevin (sre): will do. one more configurable workaround for customers: include `X-Stream-Heartbeat: 1` header to force periodic small frames (keeps connection active through proxies). we can document that while we triage.

evelyn (customer): thanks — we'll add client-side brace-balancing parse and try the heartbeat header. can you confirm whether a runtime patch to emit a final sentinel will be backported to hosted API or dedicated instances?

jonathan (eng-ml): will scope the patch now. plan: emit explicit end sentinel in next micro release and add a config flag to opt out for strict streaming use-cases. i'll post the tracking ticket here when created.

maria (support): perfect — escalating and tracking. assigning to eng-infra + eng-ml. deploy-bot: created ticket INFRA-1279 and ML-STREAM-342.

deploy-bot: ticket INFRA-1279 created (priority P1) — assigned to kevin. ML-STREAM-342 created (priority P2) — assigned to jonathan.

evelyn (customer): great, thanks everyone. temporary client fix in place, will monitor and report back if we still see failures. :thumbsup:
